translation_direction: pt → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Portuguese electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Rita and Camillo use anh/em; Villela and Camillo use mình/cậu; o senhor / a senhora is ông / bà (cô when the fortune-teller addresses Rita); narration uses chàng, nàng and anh for Villela.
decisions.rationale: Vietnamese pronouns encode the adulterous intimacy, the old friendship and formal address without added explanation.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: voltar a primeira travessa is turning into the first cross street, not going back: now rẽ vào ngõ ngang đầu tiên.
The repeated note no longer uses inclusive nhà chúng mình or the calque không chậm trễ; identical wording applied in 1.25, 1.26 and 1.28.
The cartas pun (letters/cards) cannot be reproduced; lá thư now quietly echoes lá bài.
amor-proprio is self-respect here: tự trọng, not touchy tự ái.
interesse is self-interest (tư lợi); apaixonadas is vehement (hằn học, kích động).
Restored the things/person contrast (Đến đấy là phần của sự vật…) and the intimate second-person aside with the diminutive fechadinhos.
Kept the clinical, deadpan ending: bắn chàng ngã chết instead of the added violence of quật; feições decompostas as thất sắc.
Smoothed Rita’s opening reply and had the fortune-teller address her as cô.
Removed a stacked calque in the negation sentence.
sibylla is a classical sibyl, not a Vietnamese medium: nữ tiên tri sibyl.

como eu tenho andado is anxiety rather than suffering; also lisonjeado (1.13), escrúpulos (1.19), repugnava-lhe (1.27), levo os sobrescriptos (1.23), recentes/nova (1.54) and two calques (1.31, 1.42) corrected.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: Keeps the cards (bài) central to the plot and marks the fortune-teller as a woman.

glossary.source_term: «Vem já, já, á nossa casa; preciso fallar-te sem demora.»
glossary.draft_rendering: “Đến ngay, ngay, nhà mình; mình cần nói chuyện với cậu gấp.”
glossary.rationale: Identical wording at each recurrence; fragments (Đến, ngay, ngay) echo the broken repetitions.

glossary.source_term: Ha mais cousas no céu e na terra do que sonha a nossa philosophia
glossary.draft_rendering: trên trời dưới đất còn nhiều điều hơn những gì triết học của chúng ta mơ tưởng tới
glossary.rationale: The Hamlet frame is repeated with the same wording at the opening and at Camillo’s hesitation.

witness_decision: Selected the 1896 Laemmert first edition of Várias histórias, printed pp. 9–29, from the page images of the Wikimedia Commons scan. The Wikisource pages built on the same scan were not used because they are unproofread bot text in modernised spelling. The BBM/USP facsimile of the same edition (bbm/5307) supplied only a noisy OCR reading aid. First periodical publication: Gazeta de Notícias, 1884; not collated.

unresolved_questions.explanation: Odor di femina and ragazzo innamorato are left in the original languages without gloss, as in the source.

title_review.rationale: A Cartomante names a woman who reads cards. Bà bói bài keeps both the cards and her gender, matches the recurring body term and does not anticipate the ending.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Compared the Hamlet frame, Rita’s report of the consultation, Camillo’s reproof and scepticism, and the separate routes home.
Compared the history of the three, the affair, the anonymous letters, Villela’s darkening mood and the lovers’ plan.
Compared the summons, Camillo’s fear, the cab, the obstruction, the stairs, the fortune-teller’s appearance and reading.
Compared the payment, the barcarolle, the renewed faith, the view of the sea and the ending.
